releases.title: Factor Cybersecurity Files Federal Lawsuit Against SecurityScorecard and CEO Aleksandr Yampolskiy
releases.body:
Lawsuit follows Factor's efforts to expose an alleged competitor hacking operation and alleges a campaign of retaliation intended to silence those who brought the conduct forward

WILMINGTON, Del., Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Factor Cybersecurity, Inc. and founder and CEO Jason Thompson have filed a federal lawsuit against SecurityScorecard, Inc. and CEO Aleksandr Yampolskiy in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware.

Read the complaint and follow the case here: https://factorcyber.com/factor-vs-securityscorecard

The complaint alleges that while Thompson was an executive at SecurityScorecard, he witnessed Yampolskiy and others engage in efforts to improperly obtain competitor technology and information. Thompson reported his concerns internally, including to SecurityScorecard's board, and alleges that Yampolskiy subsequently threatened and retaliated against him.

The complaint alleges that Yampolskiy told Thompson he had relationships with Russian hackers and paid individuals thousands of dollars to obtain nonpublic information about competitors including BitSight, Black Kite and Panorays. It further alleges that Yampolskiy repeatedly accessed competitor systems through a VPN from SecurityScorecard's offices, activity witnessed by multiple employees, and that information obtained from competitors influenced SecurityScorecard's product development and commercial strategy.

"Sunlight is the best disinfectant," said Thompson. "Factor is proud of the work we have done to expose and disrupt what we allege was a sophisticated operation targeting companies in the cybersecurity community. We did what cybersecurity professionals are supposed to do. We investigated, preserved evidence, identified witnesses, reported what we found and stood up for the companies and people being targeted."

Factor maintains that dozens of current and former SecurityScorecard employees witnessed relevant conduct and that substantial documentary and electronic evidence exists.

"The irony of Yampolskiy accusing Factor of stealing data and misappropriating trade secrets while Factor's complaint alleges that SecurityScorecard engaged in efforts to improperly obtain competitor information is impossible to ignore," said Thompson.

The Need for Supply Chain Cybersecurity Solutions is Real

The need for a new approach is increasingly clear. Verizon's DBIR found that breaches involving third parties grew from 15% in 2024 to 48% in 2026, underscoring how quickly supply chain cyber risk is accelerating. Meanwhile, legacy market players are collapsing under high churn, customer dissatisfaction, and notably poor security outcomes. Factor was built to address a need traditional ratings and assessment platforms were never designed to meet, bringing together internal telemetry, outside-in intelligence, assessments, attestations, and secure communications so enterprises can continuously detect and respond to supply chain threats much like they do inside their own SOC.

"While this case is an extreme example, business relationships can create real threats to enterprises and their intellectual property," said Thompson. "Factor is designed to identify and snuff out these risks, moving organizations beyond a compliance-focused approach to lightning-fast detection and response across their supply chain."

About Factor

Factor is the AI-powered operational platform for supply chain cyber risk management. Designed to help enterprises operationalize risk intelligence from best-in-class technology providers, Factor enables organizations to automate workflows, improve supplier engagement, reduce operational costs, and strengthen cyber resilience across their extended enterprise ecosystem. Through its growing Factorverse partner ecosystem, Factor provides customers with the flexibility to integrate the data, intelligence, and services that best meet their needs. releases.body:
The new offering extends LiveU's connectivity platform, giving field teams access to cellular service and Starlink broadband as a managed service

HACKENSACK, N.J., Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LiveU is now a Clarus Integrated Reseller, bringing Starlink's fast, reliable broadband directly into LiveU's cellular bonding EcoSystem through a single plan for broadcast, sports, and field production teams. LiveU Hybrid Data is the first integrated data plan that provides field teams access to cellular and Starlink broadband for the broadcast IP bonding market.

It's a shift that reflects how Starlink is being used as a primary connectivity solution across live production: not as a fallback for extreme scenarios but bonded alongside cellular to keep broadcast operations online in remote areas and through outages and disruptions.

With Hybrid Data, LiveU delivers and invoices for cellular data and Starlink in one managed service. Both connections sit side by side in the same workflow, so your broadcast can use cellular and Starlink together in the moment. LiveU serves as the single source for support.

LiveU Hybrid Data will be available for LiveU's LU300S, LU800, and LU900Q field units, across the United States and United Kingdom.

At the heart of LiveU's resilient connectivity solutions are two core technologies. LiveU Reliable Transport (LRT™) bonds cellular, Starlink, and other IP connections into a single reliable stream, trusted by more than 5,000 customers worldwide for their day-to-day live transmission. LiveU IQ (LIQ™) continuously analyzes network conditions to dynamically select the best-performing cellular operators for any given location.

"LiveU has always been focused on keeping customers live from anywhere," said Gideon Gilboa, Chief Business Officer, LiveU. "Crews get a connection that adapts to whatever the field throws at them, a congested stadium, a rural dead zone, a remote shoot with no cell tower in range. But beyond the connection itself, what our customers increasingly want is simplicity: all their connectivity solutions under a single pane of glass – cellular and Starlink broadband as a packaged service – managed and supported by LiveU, through one plan and one point of contact. That's what Hybrid Data gives them."

LiveU will showcase its full connectivity portfolio at IBC2026, Stand 7.C24. To arrange a meeting or demonstration, visit https://get.liveu.tv/ibc-2026/.

About LiveU 

LiveU is the global leader in live IP-video solutions, transforming live video into real value. From breaking news and major sports events to enterprise communications and public safety, LiveU enables reliable and efficient live production and visual intelligence at scale. LiveU offers a comprehensive, modular IP-video EcoSystem spanning the entire live production workflow. Our solutions are powered by the resilient, low-latency LRT™ (LiveU Reliable Transport) protocol and further strengthened by LiveU IQ (LIQ™), which leverages AI–driven connectivity for optimal performance. With a strong focus on automation, LiveU reduces manual processes to help organizations deliver innovative, story-centric live productions – streamlining scheduling, content creation, ingest and orchestration. Supporting digital–first, hybrid and cloud–based workflows, LiveU provides flexible, scalable and future-proof solutions that support remote productions, on-premises/cloud integration, and multi-platform distribution. Actus Digital, a LiveU company, and the value leader in its space, combines quality assurance monitoring and compliance logging in a unified, affordable Actus X platform. Trusted by over 5,000 customers in more than 150 countries, LiveU is an American company, headquartered in Hackensack, New Jersey, and a multi-award winner. releases.title: Centrus and Radiant Announce Long-Term Partnership for Domestic HALEU to Supply Kaleidos Microreactors
releases.body:
Agreement adds another domestic, U.S.-origin source of HALEU to support commercial and national security deployments of Radiant's Kaleidos microreactors

Adds another HALEU customer to Centrus' backlog and includes prepayments to Centrus that advance its build-out of domestic enrichment capacity

BETHESDA, Md., Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Centrus Energy Corp. [NYSE: LEU] ("Centrus"), a trusted supplier of nuclear fuel and services, and Radiant, a leading developer of transportable plug-in ready nuclear microreactors, today announced a definitive multi-year contract to supply high-assay, low-enriched uranium (HALEU) fuel needed to deploy multiple Kaleidos microreactors. Under the agreement, Centrus will begin delivering HALEU before the end of the decade, adding another domestic source of fuel to support commercial scale-up of Radiant's Kaleidos fleet.

The contract further strengthens Centrus' position as a leading fuel supplier for next generation nuclear technologies while expanding its role in the emerging microreactor market. The agreement includes Radiant prepayments to Centrus to support its domestic commercial enrichment capacity program. For Radiant, the contract adds another domestic source of HALEU as the company moves from its first Kaleidos test toward commercial and national security deployments, reinforcing the fuel supply it continues to build in parallel with the reactor itself. 

"The contract with Radiant marks another important step in building the domestic fuel supply chain needed to support the next generation of nuclear energy," said Amir Vexler, President and Chief Executive Officer of Centrus. "By expanding our work to include innovative microreactor developers like Radiant, we are strengthening the U.S.-based fuel supply network. This will help ensure that emerging nuclear technologies have access to the reliable fuel they need to reach commercialization and meet growing demand for clean, secure, and dependable energy."

"You can't deploy nuclear reactors without fuel, so we have approached our fuel supply the same way we have approached the reactor: build it in parallel, and don't depend on any single path," said Dr. Rita Baranwal, Chief Nuclear Officer of Radiant. "This agreement gives Kaleidos a continued source of HALEU for commercial and national security applications and removes one of the biggest constraints facing advanced nuclear deployment. We're securing the fuel supply chain alongside the reactor so that when Kaleidos is ready to deploy at scale, the infrastructure behind it is ready too."

Because Centrus' technology is U.S.-origin and relies upon a U.S. manufacturing supply chain, the enrichment that Centrus provides to Radiant will be "unobligated" – meaning that it can be used for national security applications. Centrus' AC100 centrifuge design is the only deployment-ready U.S.-origin technology available for unobligated enrichment today. Radiant is developing transportable microreactors designed to provide reliable power for remote locations, data centers, defense applications, and/or other commercial and industrial uses, representing a broad potential market for Centrus' domestic HALEU supply.

About Centrus

Centrus Energy is a trusted American supplier of nuclear fuel and services for the nuclear power industry, helping meet the growing need for clean, affordable, carbon-free energy. Since 1998, the Company has provided its utility customers with more than 1,850 reactor years of fuel, which is equivalent to more than 7 billion tons of coal. With world-class technical and engineering capabilities, Centrus is pioneering production of High-Assay, Low-Enriched Uranium and is leading the effort to restore America's uranium enrichment capabilities at scale so that we can meet our clean energy, energy security, and national security needs. Find out more at www.centrusenergy.com or follow us on LinkedIn and X.

About Radiant

Radiant is a leading developer of advanced nuclear technologies focused on delivering reliable, resilient, and scalable energy solutions that are transportable by land, sea and air. Radiant is committed to enabling a new generation of nuclear applications for commercial, industrial, and defense customers.

releases.title: A Journey into the Unconscious: New Book Offers an Approachable Introduction to Carl Jung
releases.body:
Clinical psychologist Claire Hillenbrand Sherman pairs Jungian theory with reflection, journaling, active imagination and creative exercises

OLDENBURG, Ind., Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- "Discover Wholeness with Carl Jung and His Red Book," by clinical psychologist Claire Hillenbrand Sherman, translates Carl Jung's analytical psychology into an approachable guide to self-awareness, personal growth and psychological wholeness.

Aimed at readers who may be curious about Jung but find his original writings challenging, Sherman explains the relationship between the conscious and unconscious mind through clear descriptions of his central ideas.

Jung's personal experiences, particularly those documented in "The Red Book," provide a foundation for the discussion. After separating professionally from Sigmund Freud, Jung began an extended period of introspection in which he explored dreams, symbolic images and imagined inner figures. He recorded conversations with these figures and created artwork and mandalas as part of his effort to better understand the unconscious. Those experiences helped shape the analytical psychology for which he later became known.

Sherman connects that history to concepts including the ego, persona, shadow, collective unconscious, archetypes, complexes, projection, and anima and animus. At the center of the book is individuation, Jung's term for the process of recognizing and integrating the many conscious and unconscious aspects of the personality. The goal is not to eliminate conflicting qualities, but to develop a fuller understanding of how they influence behavior, relationships and a person's sense of identity.

The book also gives readers opportunities to apply the ideas through reflection questions, writing activities and creative exercises. Among the practices Sherman presents are active imagination, a method Jung used to engage with images and voices from the unconscious, as well as journaling, dream exploration, mindfulness and mandala-making. The exercises are designed to help readers identify patterns, consider overlooked parts of themselves and connect abstract psychological concepts with personal experience.

Throughout the book, Sherman distinguishes psychological wholeness from perfection. Instead, she presents it as a continuing process of becoming more aware of the full range of one's personality, including qualities that may have been ignored, rejected or left undeveloped. By combining explanations of Jung's theories with practical opportunities for reflection, "Discover Wholeness with Carl Jung and His Red Book" offers readers a framework for examining identity, relationships, creativity, spirituality and the unconscious forces that can shape everyday life.

Claire Hillenbrand Sherman, Ph.D, is a clinical psychologist with a deep interest in Jungian psychology, eastern spirituality, and the natural world. Her career has included working at the Hollywood YMCA with at-risk teenagers, drug and alcohol rehabilitation counseling, and many years of private practice with adolescents, adults, and families. releases.title: Factor4 Announces New Integration Partnership with Tri-City Retail Systems
releases.body:
Bringing Omnichannel Gift Card Solutions to MyPOS Connect Retailers

BROOMALL, Pa., Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Factor4, a leading provider of omnichannel gift card and loyalty solutions, today announced a new integration partnership with Tri-City Retail Systems, provider of MyPOS Connect, a cloud-based retail point-of-sale platform designed to help specialty retailers manage their businesses across stores, online channels, and multiple locations.

The new integration connects Factor4's gift card and loyalty technology with MyPOS Connect, enabling retailers to offer and manage physical and digital gift cards through their retail environment. The integration supports gift card sales, balance inquiries, and redemptions, including online redemption, giving retailers the ability to provide customers with a seamless gift card experience across in-store and digital channels.

MyPOS Connect is designed to support retailers ranging from independent single-store businesses to multi-location and enterprise retailers. The platform provides point-of-sale, omnichannel sales, inventory management, purchasing, customer engagement, and reporting capabilities, while allowing retailers to connect their POS environment with ecommerce platforms and other third-party applications.

Through the integration with Factor4, MyPOS Connect retailers can leverage Factor4's omnichannel gift card capabilities to create new revenue opportunities, increase customer engagement, and provide customers with a convenient way to purchase and redeem gift cards wherever they shop.

"Partnering with Tri-City Retail Systems and integrating with MyPOS Connect allows Factor4 to bring our gift card and loyalty technology to a strong network of specialty retailers," said Dan Battista, CEO of Factor4. "MyPOS Connect is designed around the needs of retailers that want a flexible and scalable platform, and our integration gives those merchants the ability to offer physical and digital gift cards, balance inquiries, and redemption across both their in-store and online channels."

"Gift cards have become an important part of the customer experience for retailers, and we wanted to provide our MyPOS Connect customers with a solution that could support both their in-store and online needs," said Michael Steg, Managing Director of Tri-City Retail Systems. "Our integration with Factor4 gives retailers a flexible way to offer physical and digital gift cards while maintaining a connected experience through MyPOS Connect. We are excited about the opportunity to provide our customers with another valuable tool to increase customer engagement and drive repeat business."

About Factor4

Factor4 provides comprehensive gift card and loyalty solutions designed to help merchants increase sales, strengthen customer relationships, and grow their brands through physical and digital gift card programs.

Factor4's RewardOS™ API enables integrations with point-of-sale systems, ecommerce websites, payment terminals, tablets, and other platforms, providing merchants with flexible solutions for managing gift card and loyalty programs across multiple sales channels.

releases.title: Poynter, Public Media Company Launch National Initiative on the Future of Public Media
releases.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla., Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A year after the federal government upended public radio and television stations by defunding public media, a partnership of the Poynter Institute and Public Media Company is launching the Future of Public Media Initiative — a national effort to reimagine a public media system built to serve communities for the next 50 years and beyond.

Poynter and Public Media Company will guide a process based on community needs that leads to a full set of recommendations — focused on renewing public media's purpose, definition and design principles — during early 2027. The initiative will build on groundbreaking research that offers the most comprehensive analysis available of how communities across America want media to serve them.

"We're living in an era of enormous change, where technology has connected us in new ways — but also has often isolated us from each other and from reliable information," said Sitara Nieves, Poynter's vice president of teaching and organizational strategy, who leads the effort for Poynter, a nonprofit that works to strengthen journalism.

"This is an opportunity to think expansively about a reimagined public media system that can serve the needs of our country and our communities into the future," said Tim Isgitt, CEO of Public Media Company, which seeks to cultivate vibrant local media that informs, connects and inspires communities. "Our goal is to establish a clear framework for a robust public media system that helps connect communities and provide trusted information and inspiration to all Americans for free."

The Future of Public Media Initiative will work to define the purpose of public media and what it means to serve the public interest, and propose a definition, structure, funding models and design principles for a reimagined system.

It has been a year since Congress voted to rescind more than $1 billion in future funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting. CPB had distributed funding to a network of 1,500 public media stations for over 50 years, providing support for essential news, educational and cultural programming.

The Future of Public Media Initiative will engage a wide coalition – of civic leaders, public media station leaders and staff, nonprofit media and concerned citizens – in the creation of a shared framework to answer key questions about public media's future. They will use this work "to drive a recommendation for where a public media system could go and what it could look like – how it might serve the real needs of communities in this country at scale," Nieves said.

The initiative will work with a research partner, City Square Associates, which has conducted research on the needs, sentiments and opinions of over 100,000 U.S. adults.

The public sign up at futureofpublicmedia.org for regular updates.

The initiative has received initial funding from the Arthur Vining Davis Foundations and Knight Foundation. Individuals who wish to support the effort can donate through Poynter's website.

Poynter is the gold-standard for journalist professional development, and works extensively with media companies to help improve skills, ethics, editorial strategy, leadership, and sustainability. Poynter has a longstanding relationship with public media, and has worked with more than 300 public media stations — including guiding a digital transformation to increase revenue and audience. Public Media Company has worked with over 450 local media organizations in all 50 states, facilitating mergers, acquisitions, operating agreements and content partnerships that have expanded service to millions of people — work that includes launching the Public Media Bridge Fund to help at-risk stations navigate the post-CPB landscape.

releases.body:
Female-Founded Luxury Fragrance House Will Be Backstage to Introduce Its New Coastal Fragrances to Television's Biggest Stars

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This September, some of television's biggest stars will be among the first to experience La Proue, the female-founded luxury fragrance house celebrating clean, coastal femininity and the power of women who chart their own course.

La Proue will make its official Hollywood debut on Television's Biggest Night, where its newly launched Eau de Parfums, Phare 143 and Voilune, will be featured backstage in the official Emmys® Giving Suite™, produced by Distinctive Assets in support of the Television Academy Foundation.

The exclusive backstage experience welcomes the evening's presenters, performers and nominees, where invited guests include Jamie Lee Curtis, Lisa Kudrow, Michelle Pfeiffer, Jean Smart, Zendaya, Quinta Brunson, Keri Russell, Claire Danes, Carey Mulligan, Dakota Fanning and host Mariska Hargitay.  Giving Suite attendees will be the first to experience La Proue fragrance.

For La Proue founder Leighanne Neville, there could hardly be a more fitting place to introduce a fragrance house created around the idea of women stepping forward, taking the helm and defining success on their own terms.

"I created La Proue as a reminder to stand in your own strength — feminine, grounded and confident," says Neville. "To introduce these fragrances backstage at the Emmys, surrounded by extraordinary artists and storytellers who have forged their own paths, feels incredibly meaningful. At its heart, La Proue is about every woman knowing she is at the helm of her own story."

French for "the bow of the ship," La Proue was inspired by Neville's lifelong connection to the sea. Raised on the coast of Massachusetts as the only girl among six brothers, Neville learned to navigate and drive a boat before she could drive a car. Her father taught her that she deserved to be at the helm just as much as her brothers — a belief that would ultimately shape both her career and the La Proue brand.

Inspired by the salt-washed harbors of New England and the sunlit coast of California, La Proue's debut fragrances capture two distinct expressions of modern coastal femininity. Phare 143, French for "lighthouse," is a luminous floral inspired by the meeting of salt air and first light, while Voilune evokes the quiet magnetism of coastal dusk. Both Eau de Parfums are crafted with clean ingredients, hand-poured in California and Leaping Bunny certified.

La Proue's mission extends beyond fragrance. After more than three decades working in finance and venture-backed companies, Neville saw firsthand the barriers women entrepreneurs face in accessing capital and opportunity. She created La Proue around a larger purpose: helping women put their best selves forward while investing in the next generation of women at the helm.

Through the Women at the Helm Fund, a portion of every La Proue purchase supports initiatives that uplift, mentor and fund women entrepreneurs.

The 78th Emmy Awards, hosted by Mariska Hargitay, will air live Monday, September 14 at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT on NBC and stream on Peacock from the Peacock Theater at L.A. LIVE in Los Angeles.

Phare 143 Eau de Parfum and Voilune Eau de Parfum retail for $115 each and are available at LaProue.com.

ABOUT LA PROUE

Clean. Conscious. Coastal.

La Proue is a female-founded luxury fragrance and body collection celebrating clean, coastal femininity and the quiet power of women who chart their own course. Inspired by the New England and California coasts, La Proue's fragrances are crafted with clean ingredients and hand-poured in California and Leaping Bunny Certified. Through the Women at the Helm Fund, a portion of every purchase supports initiatives that uplift and invest in women entrepreneurs.

releases.title: ForwardX Robotics Launches Brownfield Automation Whitepaper: Four Capabilities for Scaling AMRs in Existing Factories
releases.body:
BEIJING, Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As manufacturers increasingly automate existing facilities, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) can improve internal material flow without major infrastructure changes. However, brownfield environments present challenges beyond robot navigation. Existing layouts, traffic patterns, material flows, IT infrastructure, and ongoing production must all be considered.

For manufacturers, the objective is not simply to deploy more robots, but to integrate automation into existing operations while maintaining safety, flexibility, reliable material flow, and long-term scalability as production requirements continuously evolve.

ForwardX Robotics' new Brownfield Automation Whitepaper identifies four capabilities critical to successful brownfield automation.

1. Brownfield Systems Engineering

Successful automation starts with understanding the factory as a complete production system. Material flows are connected to production requirements, equipment utilization, inventory movement, traffic, and IT systems. ForwardX combines material flow analysis, production constraints, traffic engineering, IT/OT integration, and deployment planning before automation is introduced. This methodology has been developed through five large-scale automotive OEM deployments involving more than 100 AMRs.

2. Engineering Adaptability

Every brownfield facility has different floor conditions, aisle widths, traffic patterns, material carriers, network infrastructure, and production layouts. Automation therefore needs to adapt to the facility rather than requiring costly standardization. ForwardX uses vision-based autonomy, enabling AMRs to navigate without floor markers or magnetic guidance. At Chery Dalian, more than 480 AMRs operate alongside hundreds of manually driven forklifts through perception, dynamic obstacle avoidance, and coordinated traffic management.

3. Production-Safe Deployment

In an operating factory, deployment methodology can be as important as the automation technology itself. ForwardX uses phased implementation, digital validation, integration testing, controlled production cutover, and progressive commissioning. Software interfaces and communication with MES, WMS, ERP, and other factory systems are verified before robots enter live production, reducing implementation risk and supporting production continuity.

4. Large-Scale Fleet Orchestration

Scaling from an AMR pilot to hundreds of robots requires coordinated fleet intelligence. At Chery Dalian, 484 AMRs operate at one manufacturing site under ForwardX's unified fleet management platform. The f(x) Fleet Manager supports dynamic task allocation, traffic management, charger optimization, and real-time fleet visibility across different robot architectures.

The whitepaper demonstrates that brownfield automation requires more than autonomous robots. Manufacturers must evaluate whether an automation solution can understand existing operations, adapt to facility constraints, deploy safely, and coordinate fleets at scale. These capabilities provide a practical framework for manufacturers evaluating AMR automation within existing production environments.

IRVINE, Calif., Sept. 1, 2026 /CNW/ -- Aurzen today unveiled the EAZZE E1 series, a compact projector family designed to make big-screen entertainment more accessible in bedrooms, dorms, apartments and other small living spaces. The lineup includes the Aurzen Roku TV EAZZE E1R Smart Mini Projector and the Aurzen EAZZE E1 Smart Mini Projector, two models built around the same everyday-use concept but tailored to different streaming preferences and regional launch plans.

Both models extend Aurzen's value-focused EAZZE lineup with a compact, home-friendly design for first-time projector buyers and everyday streamers, featuring an integrated stand, a woven carrying strap and a softer design language that fits naturally into modern living spaces.

Both models share the same hardware, pairing a compact body with native 720P resolution, 1080P content support and 160 lumens of brightness. A 180-degree adjustable stand, vertical auto keystone correction and 4D electronic keystone keep setup flexible, with an accessory ecosystem supporting floor-standing and wall-mounting options. Sound comes from a built-in 3W speaker with an approx. 80–100cc Soundbase chamber, plus bidirectional Bluetooth audio for external speakers or headphones.

The two models differ only in their built-in streaming platforms, and neither requires an external streaming stick. The E1R features the official Roku TV platform, with access to major streaming apps, The Roku Channel, free live content, Roku mobile app control and Roku Smart Picture, delivering a familiar Roku experience in a compact projector form factor. The E1 comes with a built-in Smart OS and officially licensed apps including Netflix, Prime Video and YouTube, providing easy access to popular streaming services without additional devices.

The E1R is available now on Amazon in the U.S. and Canada for $139.99 in the U.S. and CAD 159.99 in Canada, with limited-time introductory price of $89.99 in the U.S. and CAD 139.99 in Canada, and will launch in Europe later this season.

releases.body:
Baby Safety Month collaboration offers families free resources and expert guidance on child passenger safety, from vehicle choice to car seat fit. 

LANCASTER, Pa., Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As families grow, new milestones bring important decisions, from choosing a child's first car seat to purchasing a new family vehicle. Yet many parents may not realize how closely those decisions are connected when it comes to keeping children safe on the road. According to Chicco, a leader in child passenger safety, and CarGurus, the No. 1 most visited automotive shopping site in the U.S.1, the right vehicle should support proper car seat installation, provide enough space for a growing family and adapt as a child's safety needs change over time.

This September, during Baby Safety Month, Chicco and CarGurus are introducing The Family Fit Factor, an educational initiative designed to help parents navigate how vehicle choice and effective car seat use work together to support child passenger safety at every stage. Parents can access free step-by-step car seat installation video guides, expert advice from a Chicco Child Passenger Safety Technician and CarGurus' Automotive Experts, as well as a special child passenger safety episode of CarGurus' The Driveway podcast (airing September 2).

Research from both brands highlights the choices and challenges growing families face. CarGurus consumer insights find that families with children are nearly twice as likely to cite a lifestyle change – like having kids – as a reason for buying their most recent car compared to households without children. Chicco findings add another layer to that picture, with 52% of parents managing multiple car seats in one vehicle2.

"Parents want to feel confident they're doing everything they can to keep their children safe in the backseat," said William Hasse, Vice President of Marketing for Chicco USA. "With nearly half of car seats installed incorrectly3, the details matter. Our partnership with CarGurus helps parents go a step further to better understand how using a car seat correctly and vehicle choice work hand-in-hand."

As part of The Family Fit Factor, Chicco Child Passenger Safety Technician, Josh Dilts and CarGurus Automotive Expert, David Undercoffler, encourage families to consider the following tips as they start the car-buying journey:

  • Consider How a Vehicle and Car Seat Work Together: When choosing both a vehicle and car seat, make sure to identify the features that matter to you and match your needs, like installation methods or whether a vehicle can fit multiple car seats across. That way, they can work in tandem to ultimately provide the safest ride.
  • Choose a Future-Forward Vehicle: Consider how seating, space and layout will accommodate your needs today, as well as additional passengers, multiple car seats and future stages.
  • Check Car Seat Fit Regularly: As children grow, verify that both the child and their car seats continue to fit appropriately within your vehicle.
  • Don't Rush Safety Transitions: Children should progress through each stage of car seat use based on their size and readiness to help maximize protection on the road.

"Choosing a car comes with big decisions, and our research shows that families with children are going into the shopping process with a unique set of considerations," said CarGurus' Undercoffler. "They're prioritizing safety, space, and how a vehicle will fit their family's needs as they grow. Through The Family Fit Factor, we're bringing CarGurus' decades of automotive expertise together with Chicco's child passenger safety knowledge to help families feel more confident choosing a vehicle that works for them today and down the road."

For more resources and to follow along for safety content throughout Baby Safety Month, follow Chicco USA and CarGurus on Instagram or visit The Family Fit Factor guides on ChiccoUSA.com and on CarGurus.com. Find the latest car seat innovations, including the new Chicco Fit3x ClearTex Ultra-Slim All-in-One Car Seat at ChiccoUSA.com. For help finding the best car for your family, ask Guru, CarGurus' conversational guide that instantly recommends local listings personalized to your needs.

*Methodology

  1. CarGurus and NIQ Consumer Behavior and Insights survey of 3,030 U.S. new and used vehicle buyers and sellers, including 2,002 households with children, in May and June 2025.
  2. Conducted in June 2025 on behalf of Chicco, Pollfish obtained a sample of 1,000 U.S. parents with children ages 0-10 living at home.
  3. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), "Consumer Alert: NHTSA Reminds Parents, Caregivers to Find the Right Seat for Their Child," September 22, 2025.

releases.title: Fendt™ Launches 1100 Vario™ MT Gen2 Track Tractor, Momentum™ 80-Foot Planter and 300 Vario Gen5 at 2026 Farm Progress Show
releases.body:
Three groundbreaking products, including Fendt's first global tractor launch in the U.S., underscore the brand's commitment to the North American market.

BOONE, Iowa, Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AGCO (NYSE: AGCO), today announced the global launches of the Fendt™ 1100 Vario™ MT Gen2 Track Tractor and the Fendt Momentum™ 80-Foot Planter, as well as the North American debut of the Fendt 300 Vario™ Gen5 at the 2026 Farm Progress Show in Boone, Iowa. Staging its global tractor and planter launches in North America marks a deliberate signal of the company's growth agenda for the region. Together, the three products continue Fendt's expansion of a full-line portfolio and advance a common goal of improving productivity across the entire farming operation, from planting to harvest.

"Hosting our first global tractor launch in the U.S. reflects the investments AGCO and Fendt are making in this region," said Stefan Caspari, Senior Vice President, Customer Success & North American Ag, AGCO. "North American farmers measure equipment on power, productivity, efficiency and total cost of ownership, which is why Farm Progress Show is the right stage to debut the new Fendt 1100 Vario MT. And Gold Star Customer Care is our commitment in writing, protecting uptime and the Fendt ownership experience."

Fendt 1100 Vario MT Gen2 Track Tractor

The Fendt 1100 Vario MT Gen2 Track Tractor anchors Fendt's expanding North American lineup, delivering tremendous power, productivity and versatility in high-horsepower applications. A reinforced transmission accommodates the horsepower boost, making this top-of-the-range model Fendt's most powerful tractor equipped with a VarioDrive™ transmission. VarioDrive and the Fendt iD™ low-speed concept combine high power reserves and efficient power transfer with lower fuel consumption, saving farmers money. SmartRide™ suspension technology improves comfort across uneven terrain while the steerable drawbar or three-point now actively moves based on steering input, increasing tractive power and maneuverability.

A new cab with the FendtONE™ operating system adds intuitive controls, advanced technology integration and a new lighting concept for greater field visibility. A new passive cab air filter cleaning system continuously removes dust, reducing maintenance demands in harsh environments. Fendt's extensive Gold Star Customer Care backs every unit with three years or 3,000 hours of warranty, scheduled maintenance, loaner availability and parts guarantee.

Fendt Momentum 80-Foot Planter 

Fendt has further expanded its award-winning Momentum planter lineup with a global launch of the new Momentum 80-Foot, 32-Row Planter with 30-inch spacing (32R30). The largest Momentum planter ever offered, the 32R30 is designed for large-scale farming operations seeking greater productivity and efficiency.

The 32R30 covers more acres per day and reduces tendering frequency with standard 130-bushel high-capacity seed and 1,000-gallon fertilizer tanks. It combines Fendt's SmartFrame™ technology, factory-integrated Precision Planting™ systems and optional Load Logic™ weight management with a new five-section Vertically Contouring Toolbar to improve planting accuracy across rolling and uneven terrain, protecting yield potential and return on every seed. Gold Star Customer Care covers three years or 16,000 acres, whichever occurs first.

"Large-scale growers need to cover more acres in tighter windows without sacrificing the precision that drives yield potential," said Jason Lee, Senior Marketing Manager, Planters, Fendt North America. "The Fendt Momentum 32R30 maximizes agronomic performance and efficiency to achieve better yields, making every seed count."

Fendt 300 Vario Gen5

The new Fendt 300 Vario Gen5 line brings premium precision technology to the compact class, adding five models, including the new 310 Vario, which delivers 113–152 horsepower with DynamicPerformance™ (DP). Now available across the entire series, DP automatically supplies an additional 10 horsepower for auxiliary needs such as air conditioning. All models include Gold Star Customer Care, the FendtONE operating system and optional smart farming capabilities such as guidance, ISOBUS, telemetry and automated headland management.

The new updates include the latest generation of the Cargo and Cargo Profi front loaders, supported by a new hydraulic system with independent valves. Other benefits include GroundVision lighting for night work, a redesigned hood with daytime running lights and a new swivel seat.

"The Fendt 300 series has a long history of key innovations like our VarioDrive CVT, suspension systems and unmatched fuel efficiency," said Daniel Smith, Senior Strategic Marketing Manager, Fendt North America. "The Gen5 packs all of that into a compact size with an intuitive, high-tech driver's station that puts farmers first."

Product Launch Dates

The Fendt 1100 Vario MT Gen2 Track Tractor and the 300 Vario Gen5 are now available for order with first deliveries beginning in 2027. The Momentum 80-Foot Planter opens to limited orders in fall 2026, with deliveries in spring 2027.

Additional Fendt updates unveiled at Farm Progress Show include:

  • New 60 kph (40 mph) transport option, coming in late 2026
  • First-time appearances of 500 Vario Gen4 and 800 Vario Gen5 at Farm Progress Show

Fendt will also host its first-ever international press conference at the trade show in the AGCO booth #1002 on Wednesday, Sept. 2 at 9:00 a.m. Central Time.

To learn more about Fendt's full line of equipment, visit Fendt.com or visit AGCO Booth #1002 at Farm Progress Show in Boone, Iowa, from Sept. 1-3.

DynamicPerformance, Fendt, Fendt iD, FendtONE, Load Logic, Momentum, Precision Planting, SmartFrame, SmartRide, Vario and VarioDrive are trademarks of the AGCO Group of Companies.

About AGCO

AGCO (NYSE: AGCO) is a global leader in agricultural machinery and precision agriculture technologies. Driven by a Farmer-First strategy, AGCO delivers value through its differentiated leading brands, Fendt™, Massey Ferguson™, PTx™ and Valtra™. AGCO's high-performance equipment and smart farming solutions, including brand-agnostic retrofit technologies and autonomous offerings, empower farmers to drive productivity while sustainably feeding the world. For more information, visit www.agcocorp.com.

Estate Media talent Glennda Baker, Tracy Tutor, Daniel Heider, and Chad Carroll join ECHO-ME's real estate ambassador network, as the two companies expand the partnership to bring proven growth strategies to agents at every level

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- POP.STORE, the creator commerce platform behind ECHO-ME, its AI-native operating system, and Estate Media, the leading personality-driven media company for the real estate industry, today announced a partnership bringing Estate Media and four of its top talent, Glennda Baker, Tracy Tutor, Daniel Heider and Chad Carroll, into ECHO-ME's real estate ambassador network. Estate Media and its talent are now powered by POP.STORE's ECHO-ME AI platform, using AI alongside POP.STORE's storefront technology to convert their content and audiences into owned leads.

The partnership brings together two companies operating on the same core belief: real estate agents are no longer just salespeople. They're creators, and their content is already shaping consumer decisions whether they realize it or not.

Estate Media backs its talent beyond content

Estate Media has built its business around the idea that agents are media brands, developing content across personalities ranging from luxury specialists like Tracy Tutor to the most followed real estate brand, The Heider Group, alongside the viral real estate content pages that have become part of the culture, including Zillow Gone Wild, Homes with Max, Big Bankz and Houses of Celebs.

"Estate Media's talent already proves something most of the industry hasn't caught up to yet: that agents are creators, full stop. This partnership is about making sure the trust they've already built doesn't stop at the content. It becomes a lead, a client, a business the agent actually owns," said Josephine (Jo) Wong, GM of POP.STORE.

That shift was already visible from Estate Media's side, well before this partnership took shape. Its talent was seeing the gap firsthand: content performing well, engagement pouring in, but no reliable way to convert that attention into owned customer relationships.

"Our team has spent years deep in the real estate side of this business, not just the media side. We watched our talent build real audiences and real trust, but attention alone doesn't convert into deals unless there's a system behind it. POP.STORE's ECHO-ME isn't a content tool; it's the infrastructure that turns attention into business. That's exactly the kind of partner we look for," said Griff O'Brien, CEO and Co-Founder of Estate Media.

Closing the content-to-conversion gap with ECHO-ME

"Whether you're building an audience or building a business, content works best when it leads somewhere meaningful. Social starts the conversation. POP.STORE helps us continue it," said Daniel Heider.

That shift is exactly why POP.STORE and Estate Media are partnering to bring ECHO-ME's AI technology directly to the agents who are already earning that trust every day.

ECHO-ME's AI agents, built into the POP.STORE platform, close that gap directly. When someone comments on a post, ECHO-ME responds in the agent's own voice, capturing their interest in the moment, before they scroll past and move on. From there, everything lives on the agent's own POP.STORE page: listings, guides, booking, and lead capture in one branded hub. Every lead belongs to the agent, permanently, not a portal selling that same contact to three other agents.

For listings specifically, an AI concierge engages every visitor the moment they land, answering questions about the property and neighborhood, and booking a private tour or open house on the spot, 24 hours a day, whether the agent is online or not.

"The agents winning today aren't just generating attention. We're building a system that converts it," said Tracy Tutor.

A partnership built for the whole industry

Beyond the four ambassadors, Estate Media and POP.STORE plan to extend the partnership through joint educational events, Estate Media's Agent Growth Program integration, and shared content.

The Agent Growth Program already handles brand building, video scripting, production, editing, and posting for agents. POP.STORE's ECHO-ME platform adds the missing piece: turning whatever content the program produces into owned leads, not just more content.

"This partnership matters because of who gets to hear it. Estate Media has the platform to put this message in front of every agent, not just the biggest names: it's not about your follower count, it's about scaling trust and building a community of true fans who actually convert. That's the message we want the whole industry to hear," said Josephine (Jo) Wong.

About POP.STORE

POP.STORE is the Agentic AI creator commerce company helping creators and professionals turn audiences into owned businesses. Its AI operating system, ECHO-ME, powers intelligent engagement, content workflows, lead qualification, and commerce experiences that help customers convert attention into lasting customer relationships.

In real estate, POP.STORE combines ECHO-ME's AI capabilities with its storefront platform to help agents market listings, engage buyers, qualify leads, book more showings, and grow a business they own in one place.

releases.title: TOPGOLF ANNOUNCES FAMILY ENTERTAINMENT GROUP AS NEW ARCADE PARTNER ACROSS NEARLY 100 U.S. VENUES
releases.body:
DALLAS, Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sports entertainment leader, Topgolf announced today a new partnership with Family Entertainment Group (FEG), naming the seasoned entertainment operator as its newest arcade partner across nearly 100 Topgolf venues throughout the United States. The phased rollout, which began in June and will continue through December 2026, will expand Topgolf's all-day entertainment offerings with custom-designed arcade and game-room experiences tailored to each venue's local market, following a successful pilot at seven locations that delivered strong guest response.

The collaboration represents another step in Topgolf's continued investment in creating more engaging, all-day entertainment destinations. By bringing FEG's expertise in designing and operating best-in-class arcade experiences to Topgolf venues nationwide, Topgolf will continue to evolve each venue with entertainment offerings tailored to its guests and local market.

"At Topgolf, we're always looking for ways to elevate the guest experience and really be the Ultimate Sports, Entertainment and Golf Destination," said David McKillips, Chief Executive Officer of Topgolf. "Bringing Family Entertainment Group into nearly 100 of our venues adds another way to play and connect. By thoughtfully curating experiences for each location, we're giving our guests even more reasons to visit, stay longer and create memorable moments with family and friends."

FEG is recognized as one of the industry's leading developers and operators of entertainment attractions, with decades of experience creating immersive arcade and amusement experiences in family entertainment centers, resorts, casinos and hospitality destinations around the world.

"Topgolf built one of the most innovative venues in hospitality," added Rex Jackson, CEO of FEG. "FEG builds the games expertise that goes inside it. Bringing those together across 94 locations is the kind of partnership that raises the guest experience for both of us."

Rather than taking a one-size-fits-all approach, Topgolf and FEG will customize each location's entertainment mix — from interactive augmented darts experiences in bar and lounge spaces to family-friendly arcades and redemption game rooms designed to engage guests of all ages. The flexible approach ensures every venue delivers an entertainment experience that complements its unique guest demographic while expanding opportunities for play beyond the hitting bays.

The nationwide expansion follows a successful pilot program launched in May 2026 at seven Topgolf venues — Dallas, Fort Worth, The Colony and Grand Prairie, Texas; Orlando and Lake Mary, Florida; and Buford, Georgia — where FEG-curated arcade and game-room experiences were tailored to each location's guest profile. Guest response to the pilot was overwhelmingly positive, giving Topgolf and FEG the confidence to scale the program across 94 venues nationwide.

The rollout of FEG-managed entertainment experiences is underway across participating Topgolf locations nationwide, with each installation thoughtfully designed to complement the venue, its guests and the overall Topgolf experience.

As Topgolf continues to innovate and diversify its entertainment offerings, this partnership underscores the company's ongoing commitment to creating destinations where great food, golf, games and unforgettable moments come together under one roof.

Arcade Game Lineup

Drawing on results from the pilot program, FEG is curating a mix of arcade, redemption and immersive games for each venue. The lineup varies by location, but commonly includes:

  • Sports & Arcade Classics: Golden Tee PGA Tour, NBA Superstars, World Football Pro, World Cup Tournament, Quarterback Pro, Chexx Hockey, Hyper Pitch, Sink It, Pop-A-Shot Basketball (Tournament), Air Hockey, Jet Darts, Open Ice Quad and Step Maniax
  • Racing & Driving: Daytona, Super Bikes 3, Cruis'n Blast, Fast N' Furious and Jackpot Racers
  • Immersive & Themed Experiences: Halo (Fireteam, Raven and 2-player tethered formats), Jurassic Park Environmental and Angry Birds Boom
  • Redemption & Family Favorites: Toy Box Mega, Toy Box 4-Player LCD, Photoma photo booth, Duck Depot, Candy Ticket, Vortex Max XL Crane, E Claw 900, Hit the Spot, Ice Ball, Mega Shot, Connect 4 Deluxe and Grand Piano Keys
  • Bar & Lounge Exclusives: Pabst Purrfect Pour PBR and Topgolf Medallion Vending

About Topgolf

Topgolf is the ultimate instigator of play. Thanks to our 100+ venues around the globe, which are powered by industry-leading Toptracer technology, we're leading the charge of modern golf. We offer a variety of tech-driven games, a top-tier food and drink menu, space to host large events, and a vibe focused on more play for all. To learn more, plan an event or make plans to come play around, visit www.topgolf.com.

About Family Entertainment Group

Family Entertainment Group (FEG) is a leading North American provider of arcade and attraction management, custom attraction development, and technology solutions for family entertainment centers, resorts, casinos, waterparks and amusement parks. With more than 20 years of industry experience, FEG partners with venues nationwide - including Cedar Point, Kalahari Resorts & Conventions, OKANA Resort & Indoor Waterpark and The Westin Maui Resort & Spa - to enhance guest engagement and maximize revenue. FEG also owns and operates family entertainment centers under the In The Game, Max Action and Bonkers brands. The company is headquartered in Itasca, Illinois.

Contact: press@topgolf.com

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is being announced?

A: Topgolf has named Family Entertainment Group (FEG) as its newest arcade partner, bringing FEG-designed and operated arcade, redemption game room, and augmented darts experiences to nearly 100 Topgolf venues across the United States.

Q: How many Topgolf locations will be affected?

A: Approximately 94 venues nationwide, rolling out in nine phases from June through December 2026.

Q: Will every venue get the same entertainment offering?

A: No. Topgolf and FEG are customizing the entertainment mix by location — including augmented darts in bar and lounge areas and family-friendly arcades and redemption game rooms — based on each venue's guest demographic and local market.

Q: Who are the executives leading this partnership?

A: David McKillips, Chief Executive Officer of Topgolf, and Rex Jackson, CEO of Family Entertainment Group.

Q: When does the rollout begin and end?

A: The first phase began in Parsippany in June 2026; installation continues in monthly phases through December 2026, when the final markets, including South Florida, are scheduled to — come online.

Q: Why is Topgolf adding arcade experiences to its venues?

A: Topgolf says the partnership expands entertainment beyond the hitting bays, encouraging guests to visit more often, stay longer, and create memorable moments with family and friends — part of its broader goal of being the Ultimate Sports, Entertainment and Golf Destination.

Q: Has this concept been tested before the national rollout?

A: Yes. Topgolf and FEG piloted the concept starting May 15, 2026, at seven venues — Dallas, Fort Worth, The Colony and Grand Prairie, Texas; Orlando and Lake Mary, Florida; and Buford, Georgia. Guests responded enthusiastically to the customized arcade and game-room experiences, which informed the decision to expand nationwide.

releases.title: Fractal and Sky Systemz Launch Contractor Portal to Connect Construction Suppliers and Contractors
releases.body:
The new product extends the platform across the construction ecosystem, connecting suppliers and contractors through one secure, branded experience to review invoices, sign agreements and complete payments powered by Fractal.

LEXINGTON, Ky., Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sky Systemz, a software company and Fractal, a leading FinTech company serving the construction industry, announced today the launch of the SkyOS Contractor Portal, a new customer-facing experience that connects construction materials suppliers directly with the businesses they serve.

Sky Systemz and Fractal launch Contractor Portal, connecting suppliers, contractors and payments.

The launch represents an important expansion of the SkyOS product ecosystem. While SkyOS has helped suppliers streamline payments, invoicing, customer management and business operations, the Contractor Portal extends that connected experience downstream, giving their account customers a dedicated place to manage and complete the payment process, review and sign contractual agreements. 

For Sky Systemz, that means supporting not only its customers, but its customers' customers. Bridging one place to review, sign and pay. A complete demo can be scheduled on their website at Skysystemz.com

Through the SkyOS Contractor Portal, account customers can sign in using their email and access invoices and payment requests from one centralized, merchant-branded experience. Customers can see what is outstanding, overdue or complete; review transaction and line-item details; complete required agreements; and securely pay by card or bank through the Fractal payment experience.

After payment, customers can access their paid invoice, receipt and completed agreement when applicable.

"The Contractor Portal changes where SkyOS sits within the construction software ecosystem," said Brian Nichols, Founder and CEO of Sky Systemz. "We've built technology that helps suppliers simplify how they operate, get paid and manage their businesses. Now we're extending that experience to the companies they serve. By connecting both sides of the transaction, we can remove friction for the customer while giving the supplier greater visibility, control and efficiency."

Connecting Both Sides of the Construction Transaction

The Contractor Portal is designed specifically for the account-based relationships common across ready mix, asphalt, aggregates and the broader construction industry.

Rather than introducing another disconnected payment system, the portal works directly with SkyOS. SkyOS remains the system of record for payment status, while payments are securely facilitated through Fractal.

Completed Contractor Portal payments automatically flow back into SkyOS. If a supplier records an offline payment, such as cash or check, the Contractor Portal reflects that the transaction has been paid. Canceled or deleted invoices and payment requests are also updated automatically.

The result is a connected experience on both sides of the transaction: greater self-service and visibility for the customer, with less manual reconciliation and administrative back-and-forth for the supplier.

Key Contractor Portal capabilities include:

  • Centralized payment visibility: Customers can access invoices and payment requests from one account and quickly identify what is outstanding, overdue or complete.
  • Detailed invoice review: Customers can review amounts, dates and line-item details before making a payment.
  • Integrated agreements: When an agreement is required, customers can review and sign it as part of the payment process instead of managing a separate workflow.
  • Card and bank payments powered by Fractal: Payment information is securely handled within the Fractal payment experience.
  • Customer team management: Account administrators can invite team members and manage access, while individual users can be scoped to the transactions relevant to them.
  • Merchant branding: The portal reflects the supplier's branding, keeping the supplier at the center of the customer experience.
  • Automatic SkyOS synchronization: Online payments, offline payments, canceled transactions and deleted transactions remain aligned between the portal and SkyOS.

Expanding the SkyOS Ecosystem

The Contractor Portal also marks a larger strategic step for Sky Systemz as the company expands deeper into the construction value chain.

By creating technology for the businesses purchasing from construction materials suppliers—not only the suppliers themselves—SkyOS creates a new connection between the two sides of the industry's payment ecosystem.

That connection creates opportunities to solve more of the operational fragmentation that exists between suppliers, contractors and their teams as invoices, agreements, payments and financial information move between organizations.

"Our vision for SkyOS has never been to build another isolated piece of software," Nichols added. "The opportunity is to connect the systems, workflows and businesses that keep construction moving. Supporting our customers' customers is a major step in creating value in that connected ecosystem."

The SkyOS Contractor Portal launched today and is now available to customers nationwide.

To learn more or schedule a demonstration of the SkyOS Contractor Portal, visit SkySystemz.com.

About Sky Systemz

Sky Systemz is a Lexington, Kentucky-based financial technology and software company building technology for the construction and heavy building materials industry. Its flagship platform, SkyOS, is a modular operating system designed to simplify complex business operations by connecting payments, customer management, transactions and other essential workflows in one ecosystem.

Through its partnership with Fractal, Sky Systemz is working to modernize construction payments and financial technology while helping businesses reduce complexity, protect margins and create more connected experiences across the industry.

Learn more at SkySystemz.com and follow Sky Systemz on LinkedIn.

About Fractal

Fractal is a financial technology company modernizing how businesses accept, manage and move money. Through secure, integrated payment technology, Fractal helps construction and other complex industries simplify payment workflows, reduce friction and create more connected financial experiences.

Fractal powers payments across the SkyOS ecosystem, giving suppliers and their customers secure ways to complete card and bank transactions within the workflows they already use.

Learn more at FractalPay.com and follow Fractal on LinkedIn.

CYPRESS, Calif., Aug. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SKYWORTH, a global innovator in advanced display technologies and one of the top 5 TV brands in the world, today announced the debut of the C2 Canvas Art® TV, the newest addition to the company's acclaimed Canvas Art® TV lineup, available in 55", 65", and 75" models.

By making premium QD-Mini LED technology the new minimum standard for SKYWORTH Art TVs, the C2 establishes a new category-wide benchmark for performance, quality, and value in the fast growing Art TV category. The Canvas Art® TVs serve dual purposes as both premium televisions and digital art galleries.

Commitment to Custom Integration Excellence

SKYWORTH's dedication to the custom integration market extends beyond product innovation. The company offers integrators top-tier drivers for seamless integration with many of the industry's top control platforms, such as Control4 and Crestron and many others -- coupled with a focused digital sales strategy designed to maximize installer margins and streamline the specification process.

Custom integrators can also outfit the C2 with a fully customizable frame through SKYWORTH's partnership with hydroframes, available in black, silver, gold, white, and walnut, or in any custom pattern or color, with simple one-step installation over the TV's existing bezel.

"From Palette to Pixel: Illuminate Life with Art"

Michael Gleason, Director of Sales, SKYWORTH USA, commented on the significance of the C2 debut, noting: "For years, the Art TV category has required consumers to accept a frustrating compromise: sacrifice visual depth and image quality for a beautiful frame. The industry standard expected buyers to settle for flat, edge-lit QLED panels that function well as ambient art but wash out the moment the lights go down for cinematic viewing.  Our C2 Canvas Art® TV shatters this paradigm by establishing a definitive new standard for Art TVs. Rather than lowering our technical specifications to meet the competition, we integrated the advanced display DNA of our flagship CE1 Canvas Elite™ Art TV into our standard Canvas Art® lineup. releases.title: ESI Named ENR's 2026 Intermountain Contractor of the Year
releases.body:
BOISE, Idaho, Aug. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- When Engineering News-Record named Engineered Structures Inc. (ESI) its 2026 Contractor of the Year for the Intermountain region, the recognition reflected more than the scale of the company's recent projects. It recognized a contractor that has spent decades building a reputation for complex work, strong customer relationships, employee development, and long-term investment in the communities where it operates.

The award covers ESI's work across Idaho, Utah, and Montana—three states where the company has continued to grow while maintaining its roots in the Intermountain West.

For ESI, the recognition is ultimately a reflection of the people behind the projects.

A Regional Contractor with a Growing Reach

ESI's evolution from a regional contractor into one of the nation's larger construction firms has been built on a willingness to take on increasingly complex work without losing sight of the relationships that made that growth possible.

Today, ESI ranks among the nation's largest contractors, placing No. 105 on Engineering News-Record's 2026 Top 400 Contractors list. The company generated more than $850 million in Mountain States revenue in 2025, demonstrating the scale of its presence throughout the region.

That growth has come through a diverse portfolio spanning commercial, education, advanced technology, industrial, mission-critical, and other specialized environments.

But scale alone does not explain the Contractor of the Year recognition.

The award reflects ESI's ability to bring that experience to projects that are helping shape the future of the communities where the company works.

Building Projects That Shape the Region

Some of ESI's most visible recent work demonstrates the range and complexity of that responsibility.

In Boise, ESI is constructing office and parking structures as part of Micron's global headquarters expansion—work connected to one of the largest economic and technological developments in Idaho. The company is also completing major higher-education projects for the College of Western Idaho, including the Health and Science Building, which opened in 2025.

Other projects, such as The Chancery in downtown Boise, demonstrate ESI's role in transforming existing urban environments and contributing to the continued growth of the region's communities. ENR specifically highlighted the Micron expansion, the College of Western Idaho Health and Science Building, and The Chancery among the projects contributing to this year's recognition.

These projects are different in purpose, scale, and complexity. Together, however, they illustrate an important part of ESI's approach: the ability to adapt its expertise to the needs of each customer and each community.

Whether building an educational facility, supporting advanced technology infrastructure, or helping transform a downtown neighborhood, the work carries consequences that extend well beyond the construction site.

Success Starts with People

Behind every project is a workforce capable of delivering it.

That has remained central to ESI's identity as the company has grown. "Everyone Succeeds Together" is ESI's stated purpose, reflecting a belief that long-term success depends on creating an environment where employees, customers, trade partners, and communities can succeed together.

That purpose becomes particularly important as construction projects become more sophisticated and the industry continues to face challenges around workforce development.

ESI has invested in developing employees at every stage of their careers, creating opportunities for people to gain experience in the field, grow into leadership roles, and build careers within the company.

The result is a culture where experience is passed from one generation of employees to the next—helping the company take on more complicated projects while maintaining the knowledge and relationships that have supported its growth.

The ENR recognition is therefore not simply a measure of what ESI has built in the past year. It is also a reflection of the people who have helped build the company itself.

Growing Without Losing Its Roots

As ESI's geographic reach has expanded, its connection to the Intermountain West has remained an important part of its identity.

The company has continued to invest in the communities where its employees live and where its projects are built. That investment can be seen through its work in education, workforce development, charitable giving, and community partnerships.

The approach reflects a broader understanding of what it means to be a contractor in a growing

region.

Construction companies do more than construct buildings. They help create the schools where students learn, the facilities where businesses grow, the infrastructure communities rely on, and the places where people live and work.

ESI's recent portfolio reflects that responsibility. Its projects are helping accommodate population growth, support emerging industries, expand educational opportunities, and create new economic activity across the region.

That combination of growth and investment has become an important part of ESI's continued evolution. The company has grown dramatically from its early days, but its expansion has not changed the principles that have guided it throughout that journey: developing people, building strong relationships, delivering for customers, and investing in the communities it serves.

Being named ENR's 2026 Intermountain Contractor of the Year is recognition of how those principles have translated into results.

From major developments in downtown Boise to new educational facilities and the expansion of one of the world's leading semiconductor companies, ESI is contributing to some of the most significant construction projects in the Intermountain West.

The buildings may be the most visible evidence of that work, but they are only part of the story.

Behind them is an organization capable of bringing together thousands of people, decades of experience, and a shared commitment to building something that lasts.

For ESI, being named ENR's Intermountain Contractor of the Year is recognition of that work—and of the people and communities that make it possible.

releases.title: Futuri Introduces "Automate, Augment, Hold" Framework to Help Sales Leaders Avoid an AI Trust Deficit
releases.body:
Drawing on a year of conversations with roughly 40 enterprise sales leaders, Futuri CEO Daniel Anstandig warns that automating human moments produces a bill that comes due 18 months later.

AUSTIN, Texas, Aug. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Boards, investors, and AI vendors are pressing revenue organizations toward end-to-end automation, and the cost logic is hard to argue with: if a machine can do the task faster and cheaper, why not let it? Futuri's view is that the logic breaks on a distinction most automation roadmaps never make: the difference between a task and a moment. Drawing on a year of conversations with roughly 40 enterprise sales leaders working through the same question, Futuri CEO and co-founder Daniel Anstandig lays out a framework for sorting the two in "Where AI Ends and the Seller Begins."

The framework divides every step of the revenue process into three categories. Automate covers work where only the output matters and human presence adds no customer value: research, first-draft emails, CRM updates, competitive briefs, meeting summaries. Augment covers work where AI does the heavy lifting and a person makes the call. AI drafts the proposal, scores the account, and surfaces the signal; the seller refines, prioritizes, and decides on timing. Hold covers the moments where automation degrades the relationship: discovery calls, negotiations, first meetings with a new champion, recovery conversations, and the hard conversation that delivers unwelcome news. "There's a difference between automating a task and automating a moment," Anstandig writes. "The presence is the whole point. Replace the human and you haven't streamlined the moment; you've eliminated it and put something else in its place that happens to share the same calendar slot."

The cost of sorting wrong is what he calls the trust deficit, a decline that never surfaces in a dashboard, because the activity that replaced the moment still registers as activity. Customers rarely complain; they quietly disengage, and win rates soften for reasons no report explains. "This is the trust deficit, and it's the bill that comes due eighteen months after the automation mandate went out," Anstandig writes. His conclusion is that the sorting, not the software, is now the variable: "Most leaders are willing to automate. What they skip is the sorting." Two companies can run identical stacks, he argues, and "their outcomes will diverge dramatically."

The full framework, including a step-by-step exercise for auditing a live sales process, is available on Anstandig on the Future. For media companies, marketers, and AI leaders, Automate–Augment–Hold is a portable method for any customer-facing workflow, not only sales. Futuri builds on the same principle in TopLine Enterprise, which surrounds sellers with research, prioritization, and preparation while leaving discovery, negotiation, and relationship judgment with the human.

About Daniel Anstandig: Daniel Anstandig is CEO and co-founder of Futuri, where he has spent more than 16 years building AI-powered technology that helps companies transform how they sell, create content, and make decisions. He is also the founder of SparkTrade.io and holds more than 25 patents spanning AI, automation, audio, public safety, and broadcast technology.

About Futuri: Futuri is a global leader in AI technology for sales enablement, data enablement, and content automation. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, Futuri is trusted by 7,000+ companies across 22 countries. Key solutions include TopLine sales intelligence, TopicPulse real-time content trends, Content Automation, AudioAI, SpotOn, and POST. Learn more at Futurimedia.com and Futuri.ai.

releases.body:
New Agency Brings Together OM's Hearts & Science and Mediahub to Create a New 40-Market Global Network

Hearts United debuts as a leader in new business, outperforming its competitors globally and in EMEA, and topping the US ranking 

NEW YORK, Aug. 28, 2026 /CNW/ -- Omnicom Media, an Omnicom (NYSE: OMC) Connected Capability, today officially launched Hearts United, a new global media agency created through the combination of its Hearts & Science and Mediahub networks.

Bringing together two high-growth challenger organizations with complementary capabilities, cultures and geographic strengths, Hearts United is built to help ambitious brands navigate a media environment where influence moves continuously across platforms, creators, communities, commerce, and AI.

"Hearts & Science helped pioneer data-driven decision-making, while Mediahub broke new ground by proving media could serve as a creative platform," says Omnicom Media CEO Florian Adamski. "In bringing them together as Hearts United, we have created a new globally scaled network built from complementary strengths, approaches and footprints, and grounded in the shared principle of putting client growth at the heart of every decision."

The new agency - which operates across 40 markets and represents approximately $9.1 billion in 2025 billings - launched following sustained growth at both organizations. Between 2021 and 2025, Hearts & Science increased its billings by 50%, while Mediahub grew 33% - momentum that has continued into 2026. As result, the new agency debuts with one of the best new business performances in the industry as tracked by the COMvergence real-time dashboards, currently ranking #1 in the US YTD in total new business (wins minus losses, including retentions), and #3 globally and in EMEA, outperforming agencies that are up to three times its size.

Four principles define the new agency's approach:

  • Outcomes-oriented: An evolving commercial model connects the agency's success with client growth, putting accountability into the operating model.
  • Predictive by design: AI is embedded into workflows and the operating model to expand capacity, strengthen human judgment and give talent more time to solve higher-value problems.
  • Ecosystem mastery: Teams plan holistically across the platforms, communities, creators, and commerce environments where attention and influence move, rather than treating channels as isolated decisions.
  • Focused and senior-led: Expert teams work as extensions of clients' organizations, reducing silos and handoffs while bringing senior guidance and diverse expertise to the work.

Like its sibling Omnicom Media agencies OMD, Initiative, PHD and UM, Hearts United will leverage the singular advantages and assets of the world's largest global media network in scale, data & technology, identity, commerce capabilities, and talent to deliver disproportionate growth for its clients.

Hearts United will be led in the U.S. by Nicole Estebanell, who previously served as CEO of Mediahub U.S., and in EMEA by Ross Jenkins, who led Mediahub across that region. Both leaders bring experience scaling high-growth businesses while maintaining the entrepreneurial cultures and client relationships that drove their success. Their counterparts in APAC and LATAM are expected to be announced in Q4.

Hearts United joins the Omnicom Media agency portfolio as the group has the best 2026 YTD total new business performance among all global media groups for 2026 – including earning more new client billings ($4.1b) than any other group - resulting from a streak of wins including Adidas, Delta, Dyson, IBM, Mark Anthony Brands, Novo Nordisk, On, and Subway.

For more information visit www.heartsunited.com.

About Hearts United

Operating across 40 markets, Omnicom Media agency Hearts United combines media, data, technology, creativity, and commerce to help brands create momentum in a world where people move continuously across platforms, creators, communities, and AI. Built around the belief that growth requires motion, Hearts United was designed to find what others overlook, turn insight into action, and make brands more attention-worthy, crave-worthy, and shop-worthy in an AI-mediated world.

As part of Omnicom Media, the world's largest global media network, Hearts United gives clients the speed, agility and entrepreneurial culture of a challenger agency, combined with Omnicom Media's unparalleled advantages in scale, data, identity, commerce capabilities, and talent. The result is a connected growth system designed to deliver disproportionate impact for ambitious brands, regardless of their size or category.
